    `, and all four existing CSS rules. 5. **Verify** against the acceptance checks below in a browser / local file view, then hand back for review. ### Tradeoffs in plain language - **Fixed 3-up vs. responsive wrap.** The whole site is capped at 40rem (~640px), so three fixed columns give each card only ~190px — fine for thumbnails, cramped for detail. `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(10rem, 1fr))` keeps three across at desktop width and wraps to 2/1 on phones at the cost of not *guaranteeing* exactly three across. Given the site has a mobile viewport meta and a paragraph-heavy layout, I lean responsive; a strict "always three in a row" reading favors fixed `repeat(3, 1fr)`. - **Committing photos vs. external URLs.** Committing keeps the site self-contained and works offline, at the cost of repo size (binaries in git, no CDN here). Hotlinking placeholders is zero-repo-cost but breaks when the host moves and adds third-party requests. There is no existing asset convention to follow either way. - **`figure`/`figcaption` vs. plain `img` + `p`.** `figure` is more semantic and pairs captions with images for screen readers; plain markup is fewer moving parts. Cost is trivial either way; I'd take `figure`. - **Editing `styles.css`.** Unavoidable for a real card grid, and low risk: only four selectors exist today, so additive rules can't collide. But it *is* a shared-file edit that touches every page's stylesheet — the diff must stay strictly additive. ### Acceptance criteria - `index.html` contains exactly one `section.gallery` with exactly three cards, positioned inside `
